title: Phone line acceptance (17f), timed: talk 10 s, pause 5 s, repeat
note: The operator's form of the run (2026-11-20): every question is shown as text at the second it is asked, so nobody needs to hear the phone. The caller talks for talk_s after each question appears, then pauses for pause_s, and the next question comes. Times are seconds from T0, the start the runner prints. 'lead_in' is the call itself: ringing in, the consent words, the key, the queue. 'act' lines are the studio's (the screener or the harness), at the second given. 'answer' is what the unattended caller says (spoken by a TTS voice where one is available, else a tone of its own per round); a person answers in their own words. 'check' is what is confirmed afterwards from the recordings, the logs and the API.

lead_in.text: Ring in now. Trunk: dial the number. Browser: tap Call in, fill the form, tick the box, Call. Unattended: the SIP client dials.
The words have ended: press 5 (any key carries on). With the words off, press nothing.
lead_in.check: the key reaches the desk as an RFC 4733 event and the caller joins the queue; a consent record with the words' version and no number (with the words off: not asked, and no key needed)

lead_in.text: Wait: you are in the queue.
lead_in.check: the screener's card shows Phone ···NNNN (trunk) or the typed name (browser); no name from LiveKit

lead_in.text: The screener picks the caller up (T).

rounds.ask: Hello, you're through to the studio. Can I take your first name?
Lovely. And what would you like to talk about tonight?
rounds.answer: I would like to talk about the new bridge over the river, and the traffic it has brought.

rounds.ask: Thanks. For a line check, please count from one to five.
rounds.check: Whisper on the screener's ear finds one to five; the caller heard the screener (the phone's own ear on the trunk route, getStats on the browser route)

rounds.ask: Now stay silent for ten seconds, please, while I check the line.
rounds.check: the caller's level is below the gate for these ten seconds; no noise bursts in the programme

rounds.ask: Thank you. I'm putting you through to the presenter now. Stay on the line.

acts.text: The screener sends the caller to the desk (P).
The presenter puts the caller on air.

rounds.ask: And we have a caller on the line. You're on air: tell us who you are and where you're calling from.
rounds.answer: Hello, this is Morag, calling from Kirkcaldy.
rounds.check: the caller's voice is in the listener stream about the listener delay later; the phone hears the presenter and not itself

rounds.ask: What's the strangest thing you've seen this week?
rounds.answer: A heron standing on a bus shelter, very still, as if it were waiting for the number seven.

rounds.ask: Keep talking while I talk over you, so we can hear the line cope with two voices at once.
rounds.answer: I will keep talking while you talk, one sentence after another, so both voices are on the line together.
rounds.check: both voices clear in the programme during the overlap; no echo of the caller in their own return

rounds.ask: Lovely. Count down from five for us, slowly.
Thank you so much for calling the studio. Goodbye for now.

acts.text: The screener drops the caller (Ctrl+D Ctrl+D).

rounds.check: the call ends from the studio's side within a few seconds of the drop
